claims.text: The baseline MnNiSi-based alloy exhibits a pronounced magnetocaloric effect.
The baseline MnNiSi-based alloy has limited toughness and mechanical robustness.
Adding 1–3 at.% Ti and applying solution treatment at approximately 1100°C followed by aging at approximately 500°C for 2 hours will produce Ti-rich precipitates.
The Ti-rich precipitates will be nanoscale.
The Ti-rich precipitates will be uniformly distributed within the MnNiSi matrix.
Solution treatment at approximately 1100°C will dissolve Ti uniformly in the alloy.
Aging at approximately 500°C for 2 hours will precipitate nanoscale Ti-rich phases.
Nanoscale Ti-rich precipitates will hinder dislocation motion.
Hindering dislocation motion will increase the alloy's yield strength.
The Ti-rich precipitates will increase the alloy's fracture toughness.
The martensitic transformation is responsible for the large magnetocaloric effect in the proposed MnNiSi-based alloy.
A limited precipitate volume fraction and suitable spatial distribution will allow the martensitic transformation to proceed with minimal interference.
The Ti-modified alloy will retain magnetic entropy change comparable to that of the baseline.
The Ti-modified alloy will retain adiabatic temperature change comparable to that of the baseline.
The beneficial effects require Ti content to remain within 1–3 at.%.
Ti contents or heat treatments outside the specified conditions could cause excessive precipitate formation that interferes with the martensitic transformation.
Ti contents or heat treatments outside the specified conditions could produce insufficient mechanical strengthening.
